record.paper_title: Orthogonal polynomials and approximation theory: some open problems
record.context_brief: Zeros of orthogonal polynomials for singular measures
record.original_question: For orthogonal polynomials defined with respect to singular measures, what can be said about the fine structure of their zeros? In particular, determine detailed information about how the zeros are distributed and organized when the underlying measure is singular.

evidence.quote: What can be said about the fine structure of the zeros of orthogonal polynomials for singular measures?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu$ be a finite positive Borel measure on the real line (or on the unit circle) whose support is compact, and assume that $\mu$ is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure (so that its absolutely continuous part vanishes). Let $\{p_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials associated with $\mu$, defined by $\int p_n p_m \, d\mu = 0$ for $n\ne m$. Denote by $Z_n = \{x_{n,1},\dots,x_{n,n}\}$ the zero set of $p_n$.

It is classical (Mhaskar–Saff and others) that the global (bulk) asymptotic distribution of $Z_n$ is governed by potential-theoretic equilibrium measures. The problem is to describe the fine structure of $Z_n$ as $n\to\infty$ when $\mu$ is singular: namely, determine the local spacing and clustering behavior of consecutive zeros of $p_n$, the existence (or failure) of "clock behavior" (i.e. asymptotically equally-spaced zeros at the natural microscopic scale) at points in the support of $\mu$, and how the singular nature of $\mu$ (e.g. pure point components, singular continuous components, or singular parts supported on Cantor-type sets) is reflected in the local arrangement of the zeros.

Concretely: give a detailed description of the local distribution and organization of the zeros $\{x_{n,k}\}$ at scale $1/n$ (or the appropriate microscopic scale) for orthogonal polynomials with respect to a general singular measure $\mu$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of the fine (microscopic) structure of zeros of orthogonal polynomials for singular measures is an active research area. Partial results exist: clock behavior has been established for random Verblunsky coefficients and under BLS-type conditions, and local zero behavior near algebraic singularities of the measure has been analyzed. However, a general description for arbitrary singular measures remains open, with progress confined to special classes.

status_evidence.title: Fine Structure of the Zeros of Orthogonal Polynomials, I
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fine zero structure motivated by two pictures; treats random Verblunsky coefficients and BLS condition.
status_evidence.claim: Fine structure of zeros for singular cases is studied in special settings, with general theory still developing.

status_evidence.title: Zeros of Orthogonal Polynomials Near an Algebraic Singularity of the Measure
status_evidence.snippet: Local zero behavior around algebraic singularities described via Bessel function zeros.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results address fine zero structure near singularities, but a general theory for singular measures is not given.
